What are the knock-in efficiency, product purity and yield per donor, and is the γδ product shown to avoid graft versus host and host rejection?
cards.commercial_note: An off-the-shelf allogeneic γδ product anchored to a KRAS G12V driver epitope with a redosable mRNA engager to cover HLA loss addresses a real escape mechanism, but the TCR arm is restricted to HLA-A*11:01 patients and the data are preclinical with no dose, safety or manufacturing detail.

cards.title: Application of Allometric Scaling and Translational Modeling to Predict Human Pharmacokinetics of mRNA-Encoded Antibodies.
cards.summary: The authors built allometric scaling and a mechanistic cross-species translational model from preclinical and clinical data for two IV mRNA-LNP encoded antibodies (BNT141, BNT142) and found that scaling from nonhuman primate data predicted human exposure of the translated antibodies within 2-fold (allometric) and within 1.33-fold (mechanistic model), with validation against public mRNA-1944 data.
cards.modality: LNP mRNA encoding antibodies

facts.value: mRNA-lipid nanoparticle
facts.quote: Messenger RNA (mRNA)-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) platforms

facts.value: BNT141 encodes RiboMab01, a full IgG1; BNT142 encodes RiboMab02.1, a bispecific Fab-scFv-based T-cell engager
facts.quote: BNT141 (encoding RiboMab01, a full IgG1) and BNT142 (encoding RiboMab02.1, a bispecific Fab-scFv-based T-cell engager)

facts.value: Intravenous administration
facts.quote: intravenously administered mRNA-LNPs

facts.value: Mice, nonhuman primates and humans (clinical data)
facts.quote: generalized single-species allometric scaling exponents of -1.26 from mice and -0.75 from nonhuman primate (NHP)

facts.value: Multi-species allometric exponents for dose-normalized Cmax and AUC ranged from -1.29 to -1.42
facts.quote: the estimated exponents ranging from -1.29 to -1.42 for BNT141 and BNT142

facts.value: Single-species scaling predicted human exposure about 4-fold off from mice and within 2-fold from NHP
facts.quote: approximately 4-fold (mice) and within 2-fold (NHP)

facts.value: Mechanistic translational model predicted human PK exposure within 1.33-fold from NHP parameters
facts.quote: could predict the human PK exposure of translated antibodies within 1.33-fold for BNT141 and BNT142

facts.value: External validation using public mRNA-1944 (encoding CHKV-24, full IgG1) data
facts.quote: Validation with publicly available mRNA-1944 (encoding CHKV-24, full IgG1) data

red_flags.flag: Very few molecules underpin the generalization
red_flags.why: A claimed generalized cross-species relationship rests on two in-house products and one external product, which is thin support for independence from molecular characteristics.
red_flags.quote: support a generalized cross-species PK relationship that is independent of the molecular characteristics

red_flags.why: About 4-fold error from mice means reliable prediction depends on NHP data, which raises cost and time before first-in-human dosing.
red_flags.quote: approximately 4-fold (mice)

red_flags.why: The abstract does not state the number of animals or human subjects per species or dose level.

red_flags.flag: Exposure only, no safety or pharmacodynamics
red_flags.why: The abstract does not state any safety, immunogenicity, anti-drug antibody or efficacy data, which matter for setting a first-in-human dose, especially for a T-cell engager.

red_flags.flag: Dose ranges and LNP composition not given
red_flags.why: The abstract does not state the doses studied or whether the same LNP was used across products, so it is unclear whether the scaling holds across formulations or dose levels.
Concentration-time profile fit is described qualitatively rather than with a metric.
red_flags.quote: with reasonably high fidelity

open_questions: How many animals and patients per species and dose level contributed to the fits, and did the scaling hold across the full clinical dose range?
Were the same LNP formulation and route used for BNT141, BNT142 and mRNA-1944, and how would a different LNP change the mRNA elimination and translation parameters?
Did anti-drug antibodies or repeat dosing alter the exposure of the translated antibodies in NHP or humans?
cards.commercial_note: If it holds beyond these three products, a NHP-based framework predicting human exposure within 1.33-fold could shorten first-in-human dose selection for mRNA-encoded antibody programs, but it is a modeling tool and not a therapeutic asset.

cards.title: High-Throughput In Vivo Screening Identifies Structural Factors Driving mRNA Lipid Nanoparticle Delivery to the Brain.
cards.summary: The authors used mRNA barcoding to screen a library of ionizable lipid nanoparticles in mice and identified C14-306, an LNP that transfects brain including neurons, drives Cre recombination, and reduces liver transfection relative to an FDA-approved benchmark, without detected BBB leakage, cytokine or liver enzyme elevation.
cards.modality: LNP mRNA delivery (nonviral)

facts.value: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles, lead lipid C14-306
facts.quote: ultimately identify a specific ionizable lipid, C14-306, that facilitates brain transfection coupled with reduced liver transfection compared to an FDA-approved benchmark formulation

facts.value: mRNA, including Cre recombinase mRNA and barcodes
facts.quote: the lead LNP formulated with C14-306 is able to increase neuronal transfection and facilitate Cre-mediated recombination in the brain

facts.value: Brain, neurons
facts.quote: mRNA delivery to and transfection of the brain

facts.value: Mouse
facts.quote: can facilitate mRNA delivery to the mouse brain

facts.value: Systemic
facts.quote: Achieving systemic nonviral delivery of large nucleic acids such as mRNA to the brain is challenging

facts.value: Brain and neuronal transfection with Cre-mediated recombination; lower liver transfection than benchmark
facts.quote: increase neuronal transfection and facilitate Cre-mediated recombination in the brain

facts.value: No BBB leakage, no serum cytokine rise, no serum liver enzyme rise
facts.quote: the lead LNP does not induce BBB leakage, increases in serum inflammatory cytokine levels, or increases in serum liver enzyme levels

facts.value: FDA-approved benchmark LNP formulation
facts.quote: compared to an FDA-approved benchmark formulation

red_flags.why: Brain delivery by systemic LNP usually requires high lipid and mRNA doses; the abstract gives no mg/kg.

red_flags.flag: No quantification of brain transfection efficiency
red_flags.why: Claims are relative to a benchmark, with no absolute percentage of neurons transfected or protein expression level reported.
mRNA expression is transient and the abstract gives no time course or duration of expression.

red_flags.flag: Single species, no large animal data
red_flags.why: Rodent BBB differs from primate; translation to human brain delivery is unproven.
red_flags.quote: can facilitate mRNA delivery to the mouse brain

red_flags.flag: No disease model or therapeutic payload
red_flags.why: Readouts are reporter transfection and Cre recombination, not efficacy in an indication.
red_flags.quote: facilitate Cre-mediated recombination in the brain

red_flags.why: Screening and safety conclusions depend on group sizes that are not given.
Liver transfection is said to be reduced but other organs such as spleen and lung are not mentioned.
red_flags.quote: coupled with reduced liver transfection compared to an FDA-approved benchmark formulation

red_flags.flag: No repeat dosing or anti-PEG immunogenicity data
red_flags.why: PEG lipid content was varied but immune response to repeated dosing is not reported.
Nothing on batch yield, encapsulation efficiency or reproducibility of the lead formulation.

open_questions: What mRNA dose per kg was used, and what fraction of brain neurons were transfected in absolute terms?
How long does expression persist, and what happens on repeat dosing with respect to anti-PEG or anti-lipid responses?
Does C14-306 brain delivery reflect true BBB crossing rather than delivery to brain endothelium or regions of permeable barrier?
cards.commercial_note: A systemically dosed LNP that reaches neurons with lower liver transfection than an approved benchmark would address a real gap in CNS nucleic acid delivery, but with only mouse reporter data and no dose, durability or disease model, it sits at an early discovery stage.

cards.title: Performance of a modular robotic cluster matches skilled human operators for complex cell therapy manufacturing tasks.
cards.summary: The authors built a modular robotic cluster that handles standard consumables and instruments for autologous cell therapy manufacturing and report that its performance on individual unit operations was equivalent to skilled human operators on selected key metrics.
cards.modality: Cell therapy manufacturing automation (robotics)

facts.value: Modular robotic cluster of specialized modules with widely adopted equipment; robotic arm with custom end-effectors handles syringes, vials, bags, cell counters, bioreactors, incubators and closed centrifuges
facts.quote: The robotic arm uses custom end-effectors to handle standard consumables and instruments such as syringes, vials, bags, cell counters, bioreactors, incubators, and closed centrifuges.

facts.value: Skilled human operators compared against the robot on bag-to-bag transfer, cell counting, vial-to-syringe draw, and resuspension/sampling from a bag and G-Rex 100 M-CS bioreactor
facts.quote: We compared the performance of skilled human operators against the robotic cluster across multiple tasks

facts.value: Robot also ran cell isolation on a CytoSinct 1000 and wash/buffer exchange on a CTS Rotea Counterflow centrifugation system
facts.quote: cell isolation using a CytoSinct 1000 and wash/buffer exchange with a CTS Rotea Counterflow centrifugation system

facts.value: Robot performance equivalent to manual operations on selected key metrics for each unit operation
facts.quote: the robotic cluster performance is equivalent to manual operations on the selected key metrics

red_flags.flag: Only individual unit operations tested, no end-to-end run
red_flags.why: Equivalence at single steps does not show that a full integrated process yields equivalent product; the authors frame end-to-end as future work.
red_flags.quote: may provide a foundation for future integrated end-to-end cell therapy manufacturing processes

red_flags.flag: Metrics are selected and not named
red_flags.why: Equivalence on chosen metrics may not cover critical quality attributes such as viability, phenotype, potency or sterility; the abstract does not state which metrics were used.
red_flags.quote: on the selected key metrics

red_flags.flag: No sample size or statistical equivalence criteria
red_flags.why: The abstract does not state the number of runs, operators, or the equivalence margins used.

red_flags.flag: No sterility or aseptic performance data
red_flags.why: Aseptic manipulation is named as a key challenge, but the abstract does not state any sterility, contamination or environmental monitoring results.

red_flags.flag: No cost, throughput or footprint data
red_flags.why: Cost and scale-out are the stated motivation, but the abstract does not state cost of goods, run time, throughput or parallel capacity.
The abstract does not state which cells (e.g., T cells, patient-derived material) were processed.

open_questions: Which metrics defined equivalence, what were the margins, and how many replicate runs and operators were included?
Have you run a complete autologous process end to end, and how did final product quality, sterility and potency compare with manual manufacturing?
What are the throughput, cost per batch and number of concurrent patient batches the cluster can support?
cards.commercial_note: Because the system uses widely adopted, existing instruments and consumables, it could ease adoption into validated manual workflows, but commercial value depends on end-to-end and cost data the abstract does not provide.

cards.title: Base Editing of HBG1 and HBG2 Promoters for Sickle Cell Disease.
cards.summary: In an unplanned interim analysis of a phase 1-2 trial, 31 patients with sickle cell disease received a single infusion of autologous base-edited CD34+ cells (risto-cel) targeting the HBG1/HBG2 promoters, with mean on-target editing of 67.4%, HbF above 60% of total hemoglobin at 6 months, no reported severe vaso-occlusive crises after day 60 post-transfusion, and one death from idiopathic pneumonia syndrome.
cards.modality: Ex vivo base editing of autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells

facts.value: Autologous CD34+ HSPCs base-edited ex vivo
facts.quote: Ristoglogene autogetemcel (risto-cel) includes autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells that have been base-edited to target the HBG1 and HBG2 promoters

facts.value: HBG1 and HBG2 promoters, blocking BCL11A binding without changing BCL11A expression
facts.quote: base-edited to target the HBG1 and HBG2 promoters and inhibit BCL11A binding without altering BCL11A expression

facts.value: Sickle cell disease with at least four severe VOCs in prior 2 years, ages 12 to 35
facts.quote: we enrolled patients 12 to 35 years of age with sickle cell disease who had had at least four severe vaso-occlusive crises in the 2 years before enrollment

facts.value: Autologous CD34+ cells, median one collection cycle (range one to five)
facts.quote: A median of one cycle (range, one to five) was required for stem-cell collection.

facts.value: Human phase 1-2 trial
facts.quote: In this phase 1-2 study

facts.value: 31 patients dosed; hemoglobin data from 13 patients
facts.quote: A total of 31 patients received risto-cel

facts.value: Single intravenous infusion after myeloablative busulfan conditioning
facts.quote: After myeloablative conditioning with pharmacokinetically guided administration of busulfan, patients received a single infusion of risto-cel

facts.value: at least 3.0x10^6 viable CD34+ cells per kg
facts.quote: at a dose of ≥3.0×106 viable CD34+ cells per kilogram of body weight

facts.value: Mean follow-up 6.6 months (range 0.3 to 20.4); levels maintained throughout follow-up
facts.quote: followed for a mean of 6.6 months (range, 0.3 to 20.4)

facts.value: 67.4% mean on-target edited alleles, HbF >60%, HbS <40% at 6 months in 13 patients; no severe VOCs after day 60
facts.quote: the mean fraction of on-target edited alleles in peripheral blood was 67.4%, the mean HbF as a fraction of total hemoglobin was more than 60%, and the HbS as a fraction of total hemoglobin was less than 40% (among 13 patients)

facts.value: One death from idiopathic pneumonia syndrome; 87% grade 3 or higher AEs; 39% serious AEs
facts.quote: One patient died from idiopathic pneumonia syndrome. All 31 patients had at least one adverse event, 27 (87%) had an adverse event of grade 3 or higher, and 12 (39%) had a serious adverse event.

facts.value: Neutrophil engraftment median 17.5 days, platelet engraftment median 19 days
facts.quote: Neutrophil engraftment occurred at a median of 17.5 days, and platelet engraftment at a median of 19 days.

red_flags.why: Data cut was not prespecified, which weakens the statistical interpretation and invites selective reporting.
red_flags.quote: This interim analysis was unplanned

red_flags.flag: Primary endpoint not yet met at this cut
red_flags.why: The 12 consecutive months free of severe VOC endpoint is not reported as achieved; only crisis counts are described.
red_flags.quote: The primary efficacy end point was freedom from severe vaso-occlusive crises for 12 consecutive months

red_flags.why: Idiopathic pneumonia syndrome is a known busulfan conditioning risk and a death in 31 patients is material.
red_flags.quote: One patient died from idiopathic pneumonia syndrome.

red_flags.flag: Short follow-up relative to a one-time curative claim
red_flags.why: Mean 6.6 months with some patients at 0.3 months does not establish durability of edited stem cell output over years.
red_flags.quote: followed for a mean of 6.6 months (range, 0.3 to 20.4)

red_flags.flag: Hemoglobin outcomes from a subset only
red_flags.why: Only 13 of 31 patients contributed the 6 month HbF and HbS data, so the efficacy denominator is small.
red_flags.quote: (among 13 patients)

red_flags.flag: No off-target or bystander editing data
red_flags.why: Base editors carry DNA and RNA off-target risk; the abstract states on-target editing only and does not report off-target assessment.
Single-arm design with no control or benchmark against gene therapies or exa-cel; the abstract does not state one.
Busulfan conditioning drives most toxicity and limits eligible population; no conditioning-sparing approach is described.
red_flags.quote: After myeloablative conditioning with pharmacokinetically guided administration of busulfan

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing success rate or product release data
red_flags.why: Drop-out at collection or manufacture affects commercial feasibility and the abstract does not state it beyond collection cycles.

open_questions: What off-target and bystander editing was detected in the drug product and in engrafted cells, and by what assay?
How many patients have reached the 12 month VOC-free primary endpoint, and what are hemoglobin and editing levels at 12 and 24 months?
What fraction of enrolled patients failed mobilization or manufacturing release, and what were the drug product editing rates and CD34+ yields?
cards.commercial_note: Sponsored by Beam Therapeutics, the data show a single-infusion autologous product with high editing and HbF levels and no reported severe crises after engraftment, but the value depends on durability past 12 months and on the busulfan conditioning toxicity seen here, including one death.

cards.title: Synthetic DNA vaccine platform elicits potent immunity where electroporated naked-mRNA is non-immunogenic.
cards.summary: The authors made a cell-free enzymatically produced linear hairpin DNA neoantigen vaccine delivered intramuscularly by electroporation and showed it induced neoantigen-specific CD8+ and CD4+ T cells and antitumor activity in MC38 and CT26 mouse models, while electroporated naked pseudouridine-modified mRNA gave no detectable immunity.
cards.modality: Synthetic linear hairpin DNA neoantigen cancer vaccine delivered by intramuscular electroporation

facts.value: High-purity linear hairpin DNA (hpDNA), no formulation, delivered by electroporation
facts.quote: a clinically scalable platform based on high-purity linear hairpin DNA (hpDNA), produced by an entirely cell-free enzymatic method and delivered intramuscularly by electroporation (EP)

facts.value: M20-hpDNA encoding 20 MC38 neoantigens; C20-hpDNA encoding 20 CT26 neoantigens
facts.quote: An M20-hpDNA vaccine, encoding 20 neoantigens from the MC38 tumor model

facts.value: Personalized neoantigen cancer vaccination
facts.quote: Personalized neoantigen cancer vaccines (NCVs), which stimulate highly specific T-cell responses against tumor-specific mutations

facts.value: Intramuscular with electroporation
facts.quote: delivered intramuscularly by electroporation (EP)

facts.value: Mouse MC38 and CT26 tumor models, prophylactic, therapeutic and metastatic settings
facts.quote: Antitumor activity was assessed in prophylactic, therapeutic, and metastatic mouse models.

facts.value: Dose-dependent protection prophylactically and therapeutically; prevented lung metastases; synergy with anti-CTLA-4
facts.quote: leading to dose-dependent protection in both prophylactic and therapeutic settings

facts.value: Plasmid DNA counterpart and pseudouridine-modified mRNA by EP; mRNA failed to elicit immunity
facts.quote: benchmarked against a plasmid DNA (pDNA) counterpart and a pseudouridine-modified messenger RNA (mRNA) version delivered by EP

facts.value: Memory T-cell subsets expanded and durable T-cell memory claimed
facts.quote: hpDNA induces productive inflammation and durable T-cell memory

facts.value: Entirely cell-free enzymatic production, described as clinically scalable
facts.quote: produced by an entirely cell-free enzymatic method

red_flags.why: Dose-dependent protection is claimed but no amounts or units are stated, so potency cannot be judged.
red_flags.quote: leading to dose-dependent protection in both prophylactic and therapeutic settings

red_flags.why: The abstract does not state how many animals per group were used in any model.
The platform is called safe but no toxicity, local reactogenicity or biodistribution readouts are reported.
red_flags.quote: support further development of hpDNA as a safe and competitive strategy

red_flags.why: Memory is claimed but no time points or follow-up duration are given.

red_flags.flag: mRNA comparator may be a straw man
red_flags.why: Naked, non-formulated mRNA by EP is not the clinical standard, which is LNP, so the comparison does not establish superiority over real competitors; the authors concede this.
red_flags.quote: our data do not challenge the well-established immunogenicity and clinical activity of formulated mRNA vaccines

red_flags.flag: hpDNA only matched, not beat, plasmid DNA
red_flags.why: Immune responses were comparable to the existing pDNA approach, so the value rests on manufacturing rather than potency.
red_flags.quote: hpDNA and pDNA vaccines elicited robust and comparable CD8+ and CD4+ neoantigen-specific T-cell responses

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing yield, purity or turnaround numbers
red_flags.why: Scalability for personalized vaccines depends on yield and vein-to-vaccine time, which the abstract does not state.

red_flags.flag: Mouse only, no large animal or human data
red_flags.why: Electroporation tolerability and immunogenicity translate poorly from mice to humans.

open_questions: What hpDNA doses in micrograms were used, and what is the dose-response curve versus pDNA?
What are the per-batch yield, purity, cost and turnaround time of the cell-free enzymatic process for a personalized 20-neoantigen construct?
How long after vaccination was antigen-specific memory measured, and does protection persist on late tumor rechallenge?
cards.commercial_note: A cell-free, plasmid-free enzymatic DNA manufacturing route could shorten turnaround and avoid bacterial fermentation for personalized neoantigen vaccines, but the immune responses only matched plasmid DNA and the platform still depends on intramuscular electroporation devices.

cards.title: Receptor-tethered orthogonal IL-2 enhances regulatory T cell therapy.
cards.summary: In a mouse autoimmune diabetes model, the authors engineered regulatory T cells to express an orthogonal IL-2 tethered to its cognate orthogonal IL-2 receptor, giving selective autocrine signaling, Treg persistence without exogenous IL-2, and better prevention of diabetes than infused orthoIL-2.
cards.modality: Engineered regulatory T cell therapy with tethered orthogonal IL-2 cytokine/receptor pair, including Foxp3 locus knock-in

facts.value: Gene insertion into the Foxp3 locus for Treg-specific expression; vector type not stated
facts.quote: Inserting the tethered orthoIL-2 construct into the Foxp3 locus enabled Treg-specific self-reinforced expression

facts.value: Orthogonal IL-2 tethered to orthogonal IL-2 receptor
facts.quote: Engineering Tregs with an orthoIL-2 tethered to its receptor achieved selective autocrine signaling

facts.value: Regulatory T cells
facts.quote: Regulatory T cell (Treg) therapy is an emerging platform for controlling immune overactivation.

facts.value: Autoimmune diabetes
facts.quote: improved the efficacy of Treg prevention of autoimmune diabetes

facts.value: Mouse model of autoimmune diabetes
facts.quote: a mouse model of autoimmune diabetes

facts.value: Raised CD25, CTLA-4, Foxp3; Treg persistence without exogenous IL-2 in vivo; improved diabetes prevention
facts.quote: increased CD25, CTLA-4, and Foxp3 expression; supported Treg persistence without exogenous IL-2 in vivo; and improved the efficacy of Treg prevention of autoimmune diabetes

facts.value: Infused orthoIL-2 with orthoIL-2R Tregs, which failed
facts.quote: infusions of orthogonal (ortho) IL-2 failed to enhance Tregs expressing a corresponding orthoIL-2 receptor

facts.value: Claimed safe, no supporting data given
facts.quote: these results illustrate a safe and effective cell-engineering solution

red_flags.why: Constitutive autocrine IL-2 signaling raises risks of Treg instability or uncontrolled proliferation, but no toxicity, tumorigenicity or insertional safety data are described.
red_flags.quote: these results illustrate a safe and effective cell-engineering solution

red_flags.flag: No dose or cell number stated
red_flags.why: The abstract gives no Treg dose, cytokine dose or route of administration.
Group sizes for the mouse experiments are not reported, so effect robustness cannot be judged.
Persistence is claimed but no follow-up duration or timepoints are given.
red_flags.quote: supported Treg persistence without exogenous IL-2 in vivo

red_flags.why: Only autoimmune diabetes prevention is shown, not treatment of established disease or other indications.
red_flags.quote: improved the efficacy of Treg prevention of autoimmune diabetes

red_flags.why: All work described is murine; translation to human Tregs and human Foxp3 locus editing is untested here.

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing or editing efficiency data
red_flags.why: Foxp3 locus knock-in efficiency, purity, and yield are not reported.
An engineered orthogonal IL-2 and receptor are non-native proteins that could be immunogenic; the abstract does not state any such data.

open_questions: What Treg dose, route and follow-up duration were used, and how long did engineered Tregs persist?
What is the Foxp3 locus knock-in efficiency in mouse and in human Tregs, and does the construct preserve normal Foxp3 regulation?
Does the tethered orthoIL-2 construct work in established disease, and is there any evidence of Treg instability, lymphoproliferation or immunogenicity to the orthogonal pair?
cards.commercial_note: If it holds up in human cells, removing the need for exogenous IL-2 dosing would simplify Treg therapy regimens and address a known persistence limit, though the data here are mouse-only and prevention-only.

cards.title: Nanoscale artificial antigen-presenting cells reveal metabolic interventions modulate clonal composition of CD8+ T cells.
cards.summary: Using nanoparticle artificial antigen-presenting cells to expand primary murine CD8+ T cells, the authors report that glutamine antagonism raises self-renewal markers and enriches high-affinity antigen-specific clones that kill better in vivo.
cards.modality: Ex vivo T cell expansion with nanoparticle artificial antigen-presenting cells plus metabolic (glutamine antagonism) conditioning, as an adoptive cell therapy add-on

facts.value: Nanoparticle-based artificial antigen presenting cells
facts.quote: using nanoparticle-based artificial antigen presentation cells (aAPCs) as a model of endogenous expansion

facts.value: Primary murine CD8+ T cells
facts.quote: to stimulate primary murine CD8+ T cells

facts.value: Glutamine metabolism antagonism; epitope-specific TCR repertoire
facts.quote: glutamine antagonism modulates epitope-specific T cell phenotype

facts.value: Upregulated self-renewal markers, enrichment of high-affinity clones, better in vivo killing
facts.quote: skews towards cells with high-affinity TCRs and enhances their ability to kill in vivo

facts.value: Mouse, including an in vivo killing readout
facts.quote: enhances their ability to kill in vivo

facts.value: Adoptive cell therapy, framed around antigen-specific responses to pathogens
facts.quote: an easily implementable add-on for adoptive cell therapy

red_flags.flag: No dose, concentration or timing for the glutamine antagonist
red_flags.why: The core intervention is not quantified, so the work cannot be reproduced or scaled from the abstract.

red_flags.flag: No sample sizes or replicate numbers
red_flags.why: Clonal repertoire and in vivo killing claims depend on group size and statistics, none stated.

red_flags.flag: Mouse cells only, no human T cell data
red_flags.why: Translation to human adoptive cell therapy products is unsupported.
red_flags.quote: to stimulate primary murine CD8+ T cells

red_flags.flag: Durability claimed but not measured over a stated time
red_flags.why: The abstract calls the cells durable while offering no follow-up duration or persistence data.
red_flags.quote: a rapid, non-genetic strategy to pre-select durable, high-affinity T cells

red_flags.why: Glutamine antagonists have known systemic toxicity, and ex vivo effects on T cell fitness or off-target phenotype are not reported.

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing, yield or cell expansion numbers
red_flags.why: A metabolic block during expansion may reduce total cell yield, which is central to an adoptive cell therapy add-on.

red_flags.flag: No comparator to standard expansion methods such as bead or dendritic cell stimulation
red_flags.why: Benefit over current manufacturing practice cannot be judged.

red_flags.flag: No tumor or infection efficacy endpoint
red_flags.why: In vivo killing assay is a surrogate; no disease model outcome is reported.
red_flags.quote: enhances their ability to kill in vivo

open_questions: What glutamine antagonist, concentration and exposure window were used, and what is the effect on total cell yield and viability at harvest?
Does the same clonal enrichment occur with human CD8+ T cells and clinically used expansion platforms?
How long does the self-renewal and high-affinity phenotype persist after transfer, and does it translate to tumor control or pathogen clearance?
cards.commercial_note: If it holds in human cells, a drug added during expansion that enriches high-affinity clones would be a low-cost, non-genetic process change that is easy to bolt onto existing adoptive cell therapy manufacturing, though the abstract shows only murine data and no yield or safety figures.

cards.title: CFTR gene delivery to human airway epithelia using parainfluenza virus 5 amplifying virus-like particles.
cards.summary: PIV5-derived amplifying virus-like particles carrying codon-optimized CFTR were applied apically to primary human airway epithelial cultures, transducing mainly ciliated cells and restoring CFTR-dependent short-circuit current to non-CF levels when about 15% of cells were transduced, with reporter expression fading over a month.
cards.modality: Viral vector gene delivery using parainfluenza virus 5 amplifying virus-like particles (PIV5-AVLPs)

facts.value: PIV5-derived amplifying virus-like particles
facts.quote: Parainfluenza virus 5 (PIV5)-derived amplifying virus-like particles (PIV5-AVLPs) are an efficient gene delivery platform with broad cell tropism.

red_flags.flag: No sample size or donor number

AVLP production is helper-dependent and complex, yet no titer, purity or scalability information is given

red_flags.why: No cytotoxicity, epithelial integrity or vector replication safety readouts are described

open_questions: What particle dose or MOI produced the ~15% transduction, and how does efficiency scale with dose?

What are the production titers, purity and helper-component profile of AVLPs at scale, and does the platform work in an in vivo airway model?
cards.commercial_note: Restoring normal CFTR current at only ~15% cell transduction in primary CF epithelia is a relevant efficacy bar for the roughly 10% of CF patients not served by modulators, but loss of expression within a month and ciliated-cell tropism mean the product would need repeat dosing in the face of anti-vector immunity.

red_flags.quote: including severe ICANS in 4 of 12 patients. One patient developed late grade 4 ICANS temporally associated with lenalidomide reintroduction and secondary CAR-T expansion.

red_flags.why: Without a CAR-T alone arm the contribution of lenalidomide to the 100% CR rate cannot be separated from the CAR-T product itself.
red_flags.quote: open-label, non-randomized phase I/II clinical trial

red_flags.why: Twelve patients, with the MRD outcome reported in only nine at dose levels 2-3, gives wide uncertainty around response and toxicity rates.
red_flags.quote: Twelve patients were treated.

red_flags.why: All patients were BTK inhibitor-naive with a median of 2 prior lines, which is a less refractory population than typical CLL CAR-T trials and inflates apparent response.
red_flags.quote: All patients were BTK inhibitor-naive, and all had measurable disease at the time of infusion.

red_flags.flag: CAR-T product and construct not described
red_flags.why: The abstract does not state the vector, costimulatory domain, or whether the product is commercial or academic, which bears on IP and differentiation.

red_flags.flag: No dose levels or cell doses given
red_flags.why: The abstract refers to dose levels 2-3 but does not state the CAR-T cell dose or the lenalidomide dose and schedule.
Secondary endpoints were specified but no progression-free or overall survival numbers or median follow-up are given.

red_flags.flag: Mechanistic work appears in vitro only
red_flags.why: Lenalidomide effects on proliferation, exhaustion and conjugate formation are shown in culture without an in vivo model or paired patient samples described.
red_flags.quote: In mechanistic studies, lenalidomide enhanced CAR-T proliferation and cytotoxicity

open_questions: What CAR-T construct, cell dose per dose level, and lenalidomide dose and schedule were used, and what is the median follow-up with PFS and OS?
Can the contribution of lenalidomide be separated from the CAR-T product, for example by comparison with a contemporaneous CAR-T alone cohort?
Does delaying or lowering lenalidomide maintenance reduce late grade 4 ICANS without losing MRD-negative response depth?
cards.commercial_note: A 100% complete remission rate with MRD negativity in a disease where CAR-T historically underperforms would be commercially relevant, but the 12-patient single-arm design, BTK inhibitor-naive population, and 4 of 12 severe ICANS rate leave the value of adding a generic drug like lenalidomide unproven.

cards.title: Optimized Glofitamab Schedule Halves Mortality Risk After CAR T Failure in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: A Phase 2 Trial with External Control Arm Conducted by The LYSA Group
cards.summary: Final results of the single-arm phase 2 LYSA BiCAR trial of short-ramp-up glofitamab in DLBCL after anti-CD19 CAR T-cell failure (2-year OS 38.3%), plus a propensity-weighted comparison with an external control arm built from French registry and trial data, which reported a hazard ratio for death of 0.49 versus non-bispecific salvage therapy.
cards.modality: Bispecific antibody (glofitamab)

facts.value: Adults with CD20-positive DLBCL refractory to, or in first relapse/progression after, anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy
facts.quote: adults with CD20-positive DLBCL refractory to, or in first relapse/progression after anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy

facts.quote: BiCAR is a multicenter, single-arm trial in adults

facts.quote: intravenous glofitamab

facts.quote: Glofitamab significantly improved the RMST of 5 months ( P =0.007) over a 2-year follow-up.

red_flags.why: The survival benefit rests on a propensity-weighted external control, which cannot remove unmeasured confounding, yet the title and conclusion state it causally as halving mortality risk.
red_flags.quote: Optimized Glofitamab Schedule Halves Mortality Risk After CAR T Failure

red_flags.why: The abstract does not state rates of cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity, infections or treatment-related deaths, which matter for an accelerated step-up schedule.
The abstract does not state overall or complete response rates or progression-free survival in this final analysis.
Controls received non-bispecific therapy, so the data do not show advantage over other CD20xCD3 bispecifics now used in this setting.
red_flags.quote: started non-bispecific systemic therapy

red_flags.flag: Heterogeneous control arm and missing data
red_flags.why: Controls received various unspecified salvage regimens, and multiple imputation implies missing covariate data; the weighted glofitamab median OS (19.6 months) differs from the unweighted 17.3 months.
red_flags.quote: stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting with multiple imputation

red_flags.why: Only 45 treated patients in the comparison, all from French data sources, which limits precision and generalizability.
red_flags.quote: 45 glofitamab-treated patients and 133 controls

open_questions: What were the rates and grades of cytokine release syndrome, ICANS and infections with the 8-day step-up, and how did they compare with the standard schedule?
Which prognostic variables were in the propensity score, how much data was imputed, and what was the covariate balance after weighting?
How do outcomes compare with patients receiving other bispecific antibodies after CAR T failure?
cards.commercial_note: If accepted, these data could support positioning glofitamab as a preferred option after CAR T failure in DLBCL, but the evidence is non-randomized and does not address competition from other bispecifics.

cards.title: Phase 1/2 study of Trovocabtagene autoleucel, a BCMA CART, combined with ASCT in UHR MM and pPCL
cards.summary: In a phase I/II trial, 16 patients with ultra-high-risk multiple myeloma or primary plasma cell leukemia who failed or responded suboptimally to first-line therapy received ASCT followed by the BCMA CAR-T trovo-cel, with all reaching sCR, only grade 1-2 CRS, no ICANS, and 2-year PFS and OS of 87.5% at a median follow-up of 26.9 months.

facts.quote: When ASCT+CART was used as a frontline consolidation strategy, 2-year PFS and OS reached 100%.

red_flags.quote: Totally 16 patients received ASCT+trovo-cel

red_flags.why: Subgroup 2-year rates of 100% and 75% come from a subset of 16 patients whose sizes are not given.
red_flags.quote: the 2-year PFS and OS stood at 75%

How many patients were in the frontline consolidation and kinetic ultra-high-risk subgroups, and how many had pPCL?
What were CAR-T expansion and persistence, manufacturing success rate, and rates of infection or prolonged cytopenia?
cards.commercial_note: Deep MRD-negative responses with only grade 1-2 CRS in a hard-to-treat population could support a frontline consolidation use for a BCMA CAR-T, but 16 single-arm patients give only an early signal.

cards.title: Comprehensive engineering of the CasX-Editor to generate a therapeutically optimized genome editor
cards.summary: The authors engineered Cas12e (CasX) protein and guide RNA into a compact nuclease called X-Editor with over 100-fold higher editing in human cells, and showed LNP-delivered XE mRNA edited two liver targets in nonhuman primates at lower doses than published Cas9 preclinical data with no detected off-target editing in primary human hepatocytes.
cards.modality: LNP-delivered mRNA CRISPR nuclease gene editing (engineered Cas12e)

facts.value: lipid nanoparticle carrying XE mRNA; AAV also cited as compatible
facts.quote: XE mRNA was delivered to nonhuman primate liver via lipid nanoparticle with guides for two distinct targets.

facts.value: engineered Cas12e nuclease (X-Editor) plus guide RNA, two undisclosed liver targets
facts.quote: iterative molecular engineering of the Cas12e protein and its guide RNA to produce the X-Editor (XE), a compact nuclease platform

facts.value: liver
facts.quote: delivered to nonhuman primate liver

facts.value: nonhuman primate in vivo; human cells and primary human hepatocytes in vitro
facts.quote: full specificity assessments performed in primary human hepatocytes

facts.value: more than 100-fold higher editing activity in human cells; greater NHP editing at lower doses than comparable Cas9 preclinical data
facts.quote: yielded an enzyme with more than 100-fold higher editing activity in human cells

facts.value: no off-target editing detected at doses tenfold above on-target EC90
facts.quote: No off-target editing was detected for either guide in full specificity assessments performed in primary human hepatocytes at doses tenfold above the on-target effective concentration (EC90).

facts.value: published preclinical data from Cas9-based therapies in clinical testing
facts.quote: XE demonstrated greater editing at lower doses than comparable preclinical data from Cas9-based therapies that are now in clinical testing

red_flags.why: The abstract claims lower dosing but states no mg/kg or mRNA amounts, so the comparison to Cas9 cannot be checked.
red_flags.quote: greater editing at lower doses than comparable preclinical data

red_flags.why: Benchmarking against published Cas9 preclinical data from other studies is not a controlled comparison.
red_flags.quote: than comparable preclinical data from Cas9-based therapies that are now in clinical testing

red_flags.why: On-target NHP editing efficiency is described only in relative terms, with no absolute indel or knockdown values.
The abstract gives no follow-up duration or persistence of editing or protein knockdown in NHPs.
Number of nonhuman primates per dose group is not stated.
The two liver targets are undisclosed, so the clinical application is unclear.
Liver enzymes, cytokines, and anti-nuclease immune responses are not mentioned for an engineered bacterial protein.
The text claims compatibility with AAV but reports in vivo data only with LNP.
red_flags.quote: for delivery using adeno-associated virus (AAV) or lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery strategies

red_flags.why: Specificity was tested in primary human hepatocytes, not in the treated animals, and chromosomal rearrangements or translocations are not mentioned.
red_flags.quote: full specificity assessments performed in primary human hepatocytes

red_flags.why: No yield, purity, or mRNA/LNP process information is given.

open_questions: What absolute editing percentages and doses in mg/kg were achieved at each of the two NHP liver targets, and with how many animals per group?
How long was editing and target protein reduction followed in NHPs, and were liver enzymes and immune responses measured?
Which off-target detection methods were used, and were translocations, large deletions, and in vivo tissue biodistribution assessed?
cards.commercial_note: A compact, highly specific nuclease that works at lower LNP doses than Cas9 and could fit in AAV would be attractive both as an in vivo editing platform and as a licensable alternative to crowded Cas9 IP, but the abstract names no indication and gives no dose numbers.

cards.title: Spatial Regulation of CAR Signaling Enables Logic-Gated Activity
cards.summary: The authors describe MANTIS, an AND-gated chimeric antigen receptor in which a bulky extracellular blocking domain sterically prevents CAR signaling until a first antigen triggers shedding of that domain, after which binding of a second antigen activates the T cell.
cards.modality: CAR-T cell therapy with engineered logic-gated receptor

facts.value: Engineered receptor design named MANTIS expressed in T cells; delivery method not stated
facts.quote: we design a fundamentally new AND-gated receptor called M ulti- AN tigen T riggered I mmune S ynapse (MANTIS)

facts.value: Two antigens required in an AND gate; specific antigens not named
facts.quote: releasing a free CAR that can bind a second antigen and activate the T cell in an AND-gated manner

facts.value: Cancer, framed around avoiding killing of normal cells sharing antigens
facts.quote: Chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) can induce T cells to kill cancer cells but also to kill normal cells that express the same antigens

facts.value: T cells; autologous or allogeneic not stated
facts.quote: Creating such AND-gated CAR T cells has been challenging

red_flags.flag: No in vivo or animal data stated
red_flags.why: The abstract reports only receptor behavior and gives no model, species or tumor challenge experiment.
Without specific antigen pairs it is impossible to judge which tumor indications are addressable or whether the expression differentials are real.
No killing percentages, cytokine levels, or leakiness measurements of the OFF state are given, so the tightness of the AND gate is unknown.
red_flags.quote: MANTIS initially prevents CAR activity by steric blocking with a bulky extracellular domain.

red_flags.flag: No safety or on-target off-tumor data
red_flags.why: The entire premise is improved specificity, yet no data on normal cell sparing are stated.
Shedding-based receptors may be irreversibly activated once the blocking domain is lost, and no timecourse is mentioned.
red_flags.quote: MANTIS sheds this blocking domain

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing, transduction efficiency or yield data
red_flags.why: A multi-domain receptor adds construct size and expression burden, and the abstract gives no production detail.

red_flags.flag: Potential antigen spreading of the shed domain state
red_flags.why: Once shedding occurs, a free CAR exists that may act independently of the first antigen in other tissues; the abstract does not address spatial confinement.
red_flags.quote: releasing a free CAR that can bind a second antigen and activate the T cell

open_questions: Which antigen pairs were tested, and what is the baseline leakiness of the CAR in the absence of the first antigen?
Is the shedding event local and reversible, or does a cell that has encountered antigen A once remain permanently armed against antigen B elsewhere?
Has the system been tested in vivo against a tumor plus a normal tissue expressing only one antigen?
cards.commercial_note: If the gate is tight, a size-based AND gate would widen the set of targetable antigens beyond tumor-exclusive ones, but the abstract names no antigen pair, no indication and no in vivo result, so the commercial case is unproven.

cards.title: Novel Engineered AAV Variants Demonstrate Superior Blood-Brain Barrier Penetration and Safety in Non-Human Primates
cards.summary: The authors report engineered AAV capsids from a proprietary platform (REACH) that, after intravenous dosing in non-human primates, gave brain transgene RNA levels 600-2000 fold above AAV9 with 10-50 fold lower liver tropism.
cards.modality: AAV gene therapy (engineered capsid, systemic CNS delivery)

facts.value: Novel engineered AAV capsid variants from the REACH platform
facts.quote: we report the development of novel AAV variants via a proprietary capsid engineering platform (REACH)

facts.value: CNS/neurological disorders, broadly stated
facts.quote: a transformative platform for treating a broad spectrum of neurological diseases

facts.quote: 600-2000 fold higher than AAV9

red_flags.quote: 600-2000 fold higher than AAV9 at the RNA level

No follow-up time or persistence of expression is given.
"minimal off-target exposure" and "markedly improved safety profile" are asserted without liver enzymes, histopathology or DRG pathology scores.
red_flags.quote: a markedly improved safety profile

red_flags.flag: No immunogenicity or pre-existing neutralizing antibody data

Engineered capsids frequently have poor packaging titer or purity; nothing is reported.

red_flags.flag: No disease model or efficacy endpoint
red_flags.why: Only biodistribution-type readouts in healthy NHPs; no therapeutic payload tested in a disease setting.

cards.title: Structural dynamics insights into principles underlying the fitness of new broadly potent AAVs

cards.title: A minimally modified AAV9 variant (AAV9fyhr) for enhanced CNS gene delivery by intra-CSF administration

red_flags.why: Outperforming clinically relevant vectors is claimed without naming them or giving a magnitude.
red_flags.quote: outperforming clinically relevant vectors with minimal off-target expression

red_flags.why: Reconstitution rate and the fraction of IHCs expressing full-length otoferlin are not given numerically; partial products and mis-splicing are not addressed.
red_flags.quote: efficient dual-AAV trans-splicing delivery of the large OTOF gene

red_flags.flag: No biodistribution or systemic safety data
red_flags.why: The abstract does not state vector spread to brain, liver or contralateral ear beyond a general minimal off-target claim.
Packaging efficiency is called superior but no titer or yield figures are stated.

open_questions: What vector genome dose per ear was used in mice and in non-human primates, and what is the dose response for ABR threshold recovery?
How long was hearing followed after treatment, and did otoferlin expression or thresholds decline over that period?

What fraction of IHCs express full-length reconstituted otoferlin versus truncated trans-splicing products, and what is the capsid's neutralization profile against pre-existing human anti-AAV2 antibodies?
cards.commercial_note: An AAV capsid with selective inner hair cell tropism at low dose that works in non-human primates after round window delivery and supports dual-vector OTOF delivery could underpin an OTOF program and be licensed as a platform for other hearing loss genes, but the absence of dose, durability and immunogenicity numbers leaves its edge over existing clinical vectors unproven.

cards.title: A Standalone PD-1 Chimeric Switch Receptor T-Cell Platform Expands the Therapeutic Window of PD-L1 Targeting in Solid Tumors
cards.summary: The authors engineered PD-1 chimeric switch receptor T cells targeting PD-L1 and report retained tumor and myeloid cell killing with reduced killing of several primary normal human cell types, plus tumor control in orthotopic breast cancer and patient-derived glioblastoma mouse models.
cards.modality: Engineered T-cell therapy (PD-1 chimeric switch receptor T cells)

facts.value: PD-1 chimeric switch receptor construct in T cells
facts.quote: we developed a standalone programmed death-1 (PD-1) chimeric switch receptor (CSR) T-cell platform

facts.value: PD-L1 on tumor and myeloid cells
facts.quote: retained potent PD-L1-specific cytotoxicity against tumor cells

facts.value: Solid tumors, specifically breast cancer and glioblastoma
facts.quote: suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival in orthotopic breast cancer and patient-derived glioblastoma models

facts.value: 3D multicellular tumor organoids plus two in vivo tumor models
facts.quote: three-dimensional (3D) multicellular tumor organoids

facts.value: Systemic for breast model, intracranial for glioblastoma model
facts.quote: after systemic and intracranial administration, respectively

facts.value: Tumor growth suppression and longer survival in both in vivo models
facts.quote: both candidates suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival

facts.value: Lower killing of primary human small airway epithelial cells, astrocytes, renal epithelial cells, hepatocytes and cardiomyocytes versus antibody-based PD-L1 CAR T
facts.quote: exhibiting markedly reduced cytotoxicity against primary human small airway epithelial cells, astrocytes, renal epithelial cells, hepatocytes, and cardiomyocytes

facts.value: Previously developed antibody-based PD-L1 CAR T cells
facts.quote: Compared with our previously developed antibody-based PD-L1 CAR T cells

red_flags.flag: No dose or cell number stated
red_flags.why: T-cell dose drives both efficacy and toxicity and cannot be judged here.
The abstract does not state animal numbers or replicate counts for any experiment.

red_flags.flag: Safety claim rests on in vitro primary cell killing, not in vivo toxicology
red_flags.why: Reduced cytotoxicity against cultured normal cells does not establish an improved therapeutic window in a system with physiological PD-L1 expression, and mouse models poorly model human normal tissue PD-L1.
red_flags.quote: exhibiting markedly reduced cytotoxicity against primary human small airway epithelial cells, astrocytes, renal epithelial cells, hepatocytes, and cardiomyocytes

red_flags.why: The abstract gives no follow-up duration, T-cell persistence, or relapse data beyond survival prolongation.

red_flags.flag: Mechanistic concern with PD-1 based binders not addressed
red_flags.why: A PD-1 ectodomain binds PD-L2 and has lower affinity, so specificity and off-target binding to PD-L2 bearing tissue is unclear and the abstract does not state it.

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing, yield or transduction data
red_flags.why: Nothing on vector, transduction efficiency, expansion or product phenotype is reported.
"suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival" without magnitudes, cure rates or statistics makes the effect size unknowable.
red_flags.quote: both candidates suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival

open_questions: What cell doses were used in each model, and what are the tumor growth and survival effect sizes with group sizes?
Was any in vivo toxicity study done in a system with human or cross-reactive PD-L1 expression in normal tissue, and does the CSR bind PD-L2?
Do the CSR T cells persist and resist exhaustion, and is there rechallenge or long-term durability data?
cards.commercial_note: PD-L1 is broadly expressed across solid tumors and the dual tumor plus myeloid targeting plus a claimed safety margin over an existing antibody-based PD-L1 CAR would matter if the window holds in vivo, but with no dose, durability or toxicology detail this is early preclinical.

cards.title: RNA-Encoded PGT121-LS Anti-HIV Antibody: Comprehensive Preclinical Characterization and Translational Pharmacokinetics
cards.summary: The authors delivered mRNA-LNPs encoding the HIV bNAb PGT121 and Fc variants, showing in vitro neutralization, expression in mice and NHPs, well tolerated IV dosing without anti-drug antibodies over 180 days but ADA and lower bioavailability after IM dosing, plus a PK model for first-in-human dose prediction.
cards.modality: LNP-delivered mRNA encoding a broadly neutralizing antibody

facts.value: lipid nanoparticle delivered RNA
facts.quote: enables in vivo antibody production of the clinically validated bNAb PGT121 via lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery

facts.value: PGT121 bNAb with Fc variants LS, del294, LS-del294
facts.quote: supporting rapid evaluation of Fc variants (LS, del294, LS-del294) in vitro and in vivo

facts.value: HIV-1
facts.quote: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)-1 broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) have demonstrated clinical efficacy

facts.value: mice and non-human primates
facts.quote: In mice, single RNA-LNP administrations yielded in vivo expression of all RibobNAb variants

facts.value: single intravenous; also single intramuscular
facts.quote: a single intravenous administration of PGT121-LS RNA-LNP was well tolerated

facts.value: NHP follow-up 180 days; ADA from Day 14 after IM
facts.quote: without anti-drug antibody (ADA) formation over 180 days

facts.value: sub-nanomolar Env binding and potent neutralization in vitro; in vivo expressed antibody matched reference protein function
facts.quote: We confirmed expression, sub-nanomolar HIV-1 Env binding, and potent neutralization across all RibobNAb variants in vitro.

facts.value: IV dosing well tolerated, no ADA; IM dosing led to ADA
facts.quote: Single intramuscular administration showed RibobNAb expression but resulted in ADA development from Day 14 onwards and lower bioavailability.

facts.value: PGT121-LS recombinant reference protein
facts.quote: resulted in PGT121-LS half-lives comparable to the reference protein

facts.value: framed as avoiding recombinant protein production and purification
facts.quote: face manufacturing challenges associated with recombinant protein production and purification

red_flags.why: No RNA-LNP dose level or mg/kg is given for mice or NHP, so expression per dose and the human dose projection cannot be judged.
The abstract does not state how many mice or NHPs were used per arm.
ADA from Day 14 plus lower bioavailability undercuts the convenient route that would be needed for prophylaxis at scale.
red_flags.quote: resulted in ADA development from Day 14 onwards and lower bioavailability

red_flags.flag: No in vivo antiviral protection data
red_flags.why: Efficacy is binding and neutralization in vitro plus expression in vivo; no SHIV challenge or viral load endpoint is reported.
red_flags.quote: In vivo-expressed PGT121-LS RibobNAb retained identical antiviral functionality to PGT121-LS reference protein.

red_flags.why: Half-life is described but achieved antibody titers versus the protective threshold are not stated.
Chronic HIV prophylaxis or therapy would need repeat administration, and only single administrations are described.
red_flags.quote: single RNA-LNP administrations

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing or yield data despite manufacturing being the stated rationale
red_flags.why: The abstract claims a manufacturing advantage but gives no RNA or LNP production, cost or yield figures.

open_questions: What RNA-LNP doses were used in mice and NHPs, and what peak and trough serum PGT121-LS concentrations were achieved relative to the protective threshold?
What drives ADA after IM but not IV dosing, and can repeat dosing be done without loss of expression?
What first-in-human dose did the allometric model predict, and how does the required RNA amount compare on cost to recombinant PGT121-LS?
cards.commercial_note: If a single IV RNA-LNP dose can give protein-comparable half-life without ADA over 180 days, it offers a route to bNAb delivery that avoids recombinant protein manufacturing, but the IM ADA finding limits the low-cost outpatient route that HIV prophylaxis markets would need.

cards.title: Mechanically-mediated low-pressure cell membrane poration enables tunable intracellular delivery of traditionally impermeable cargoes in high throughput and clinical scale formats
cards.summary: The authors describe a mechanical, low-pressure cell membrane poration platform for passive-diffusion intracellular delivery of otherwise impermeable cargoes, and report example applications in live-cell DNA-encoded library discovery, cell therapy manufacturing, and primary cell assays.
cards.modality: Non-viral mechanical cell membrane poration for intracellular delivery (ex vivo cell engineering)

facts.value: Mechanically-mediated low-pressure poration platform relying on passive diffusion
facts.quote: We designed a mechanically-mediated poration platform governed by deterministic, passive diffusion operating at low pressure

facts.value: Cargo-agnostic; traditionally impermeable cargoes, with multiplexing
facts.quote: enables dose-dependent, cargo-agnostic intracellular delivery and preserves cellular homeostasis; key advantages include high-fidelity multiplexing, transient cell engineering

facts.value: Includes sensitive primary cell types
facts.quote: assay development in sensitive primary cell types

facts.value: Claimed high throughput and clinical scale formats, with rapid cell therapy manufacturing shown
facts.quote: complex and rapid cell therapy manufacturing

red_flags.flag: No quantitative data of any kind
red_flags.why: The abstract gives no delivery efficiency, viability, dose, throughput or scale numbers, so claims cannot be assessed.
Terms like cargo-agnostic, deterministic and clinical scale are asserted rather than supported with stated evidence.
red_flags.quote: deterministic, passive diffusion operating at low pressure which enables dose-dependent, cargo-agnostic intracellular delivery

red_flags.flag: No named cell types or species
red_flags.why: Only "sensitive primary cell types" is stated; no specific human cells, donor numbers or species are given.
red_flags.quote: assay development in sensitive primary cell types

red_flags.flag: No sample size or replicate information
red_flags.why: The abstract does not state how many runs, donors or cell batches were tested.
Manufacturing is claimed but no transduction/editing rate, phenotype, potency or in vivo result is stated.
red_flags.quote: complex and rapid cell therapy manufacturing

red_flags.why: Traditional methods such as electroporation are criticized but no head-to-head result is reported.
red_flags.quote: Traditional intracellular delivery methods suffer from cargo inefficiencies, non-linear delivery kinetics, and cellular trauma.

red_flags.why: The abstract mentions transient engineering but gives no time course or stability measurements.

red_flags.flag: No manufacturing yield, throughput rate or cost data
red_flags.why: Clinical scale is claimed without cells per hour, recovery or GMP information.
red_flags.quote: high throughput and clinical scale formats

open_questions: What delivery efficiency and post-treatment viability do you measure, by cargo class and by cell type, versus electroporation?
What are the actual throughput and cell numbers processed in the clinical scale format, and what is cell recovery?
For the cell therapy example, what editing or expression levels and functional potency were achieved, and over what time course?
cards.commercial_note: A cargo-agnostic, low-trauma delivery device spanning drug discovery screening and cell therapy manufacturing could serve two revenue channels, but the abstract supplies no efficiency, viability, throughput or comparator numbers to judge whether it beats electroporation.
